subject: India
note: Cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary): Indian plate. The drift is drawn from a published plate-motion model (public/geo plates); ages are the article's, and the article notes the collision's start is debated (as early as 55 million years ago).

claims.text: Originally a part of the ancient continent of Gondwana, the Indian plate broke away from the other fragments of Gondwana 100 million years ago and began moving north, carrying Insular India with it.
It began moving north at about 20 cm per year.
It is believed to have begun colliding with Asia as early as 55 million years ago.
The collision with the Eurasian plate formed the orogenic belt that created the Tibetan Plateau and the Himalaya Mountains.
